TextEng: This young, imposing wizard has long, flowing hair that has turned prematurely white.
Aerel is a grim wolf of man who surveys his inn with an eagle eye.
This half-elf is a rare beauty with a laugh like liquid moonlight.
There is something oddly familiar about this mage. You can't quite put your finger on it.
Amaril Sweetwater is a half-elf of wood elf stock, a former adventuress and reputedly a tough businesswoman.
Amberlyn could well have been beautiful once, but the advancing years, together with the permanent frown on her face, have taken their toll.

Whatever god these priests worship, he is powerful enough to grant them full access to a host of cleric spells. Once he's finished attempting to incapacitate enemies from a distance, the typical Order priest will close in attack with his spiked mace. Defensively, they carry huge tower shields and wear full plate amor under their robes.

The typical Order warrior appears to be a veteran fighter, using a sword and shield style combat style and wearing half-plate armor beneath his ominous black robe. They fight with far more skill than would would expect from a typical cultist.

The most dangerous of those that make up the Order, these wizards are clothed in dark robes like the rest of the group. They possess a deadly arsenal of destructive spells and seem to be a par with the most experienced Purple Cloaks of Mulmaster and War Wizards of Cormyr in terms of power.
Angrym is a ranger and reputedly a fine judge of horseflesh.
The Hillsfar Arena announcer is an aging, dapper man with a cruel smile and a taste for depravity - unsurprising in one who is part of the Innovator of Pain's personal staff.

This small, slender man is perfectly toned and carries not an ounce of fat. His thick, raven-black hair and controlled stubble would lead many to believe him handsome, were it not for those dead gray eyes: windows into his empty soul. This man is a killer of unsurpassed skill.
Tall and muscular, with steely gray hair and blue eyes to match, Astar is every inch the formidable fighter. He's in perfect physical shape despite his forty-odd years.
The legendary pirate king Avagard must be nearing his seventieth year, but he remains in excellent physical condition and is a commanding presence. Though, there is something odd about his eyes...
Baerimel is the younger of the two sisters. She has obviously been mistreated, though to what extent, you cannot be certain.
For all of his sword-waving and boastful proclamations, there is a terrified look in this young man's eyes.
Created from the fanatical worshippers of the god Bane, these hateful undead possess surprising cunning and often work together to take down their prey.
These animated skeletons are created by powerful priests of Bane and used as undead guardians. Intelligent and malevolent, they use magic in addition to melee attacks.
This ruddy-faced man is laughing and joking with the tavern patrons. His clothes are covered in ale stains.
Beirmoura is the famed Bright Sword of Thentia, a sentient weapon created over a thousand years ago to combat the wizards of Netheril.

Lashan's father is a man in his early fifties, whose recent imprisonment has left him looking a good deal older. His body is covered with bruises and the cloth tunic he once wore is now little more than rags.

Lashan's father is a man in his early fifties, whose recent imprisonment has left him looking a good deal older. His body is covered with bruises and the cloth tunic he once wore is now little more than rags.
This lazy half-orc has intractable body odor.
An angry young woman, Blizzard's arsenal of cold-related spells are the source of her nickname. She seems reluctant to speak about her life before the Arena.

This solid-looking man appears to be in his late thirties. His long, drab robes cover his powerful frame, and the plain oaken staff he carries looks strong enough to crack skulls if the need arises. Despite that, he is obviously a man of peace rather than violence.
This wicked-looking half-orc wears his evil grin proudly.
The typical Zhentarim fighter is a skilled warrior, cruel yet disciplined.

The early days of the Banedeath did not go well for Cyric, and many of his fledgling clerics were slaughtered at the hands of powerful Banites. Cyric soon after empowered select members of his clerical faithful with a portion of his power - so much power, in fact - that these clerics' mortal forms dissolved into nothing more than mere bones and the fiery power of the Dark Sun.

The captain of the Red Plume force stationed at Yûlash is a hard, cruel-looking man of middling years. Haliator has a reputation for turning a blind eye to looting and extortion, providing it's the Red Plumes doing it.
A tall, commanding woman, Kettia is an exotic beauty despite the scars covering her face. The crew of the Grim Voyager obey her orders without a moment's hesitation.
This forty-something warrior appears to be a captain in the Zhentarim forces. She has a haunted look in her eyes, gazing around with a nervousness you wouldn't expect from a seasoned warrior.
Captain Zamakus is a commanding warrior, and deadly serious about ensuring the smooth passage of the Thayan visit.
Roses are carved the length of the quarterstaff held by this weathered old priest.
The head priest of the Hall of the Unicorn is an aging half-elf of noble bearing and great wisdom. His widow's peak frames a face that is starting to show heavy laughter-lines.
Priests of the Dark Lord Bane are feared throughout the Moonsea for their cruelty and love of strife.
This tall, taciturn warrior guards the temple from would-be thieves. Though her manner is no-nonsense, there is a softness to her eyes and voice that hint she is more compassionate than she lets on.
This bard strums his harp with mechanical precision.
This old woman yells orders at her maids as she valiantly attempts to keep the patrons of the overcrowded inn well fed.
This shady, hooded figure is clearly bad news.

This huge bear of a man looks as wild and primeval as the surrounding forest. His weathered skin and large, knotted muscles tell of his many years spent in the wild, and his enormous greataxe looks as though it has seen a considerable amount of use.
This old man looks crazed. His filthy clothes haven't been washed in many days, and his grimy face stares with an expression of pure, illogical hatred.
A typical citizen of Elventree. While many of the inhabitants of the small settlement are Harpers, rangers, or druids, a greater number are simple craftsmen, artists, or merchants.
This forlorn-looking woman wears tattered clothes, her filthy hair framing a malnourished face.
A typical citizen of Elventree. While many of the inhabitants of the small settlement are Harpers, rangers, or druids, a greater number are simple craftsmenm, artists, or merchants.

This venerable wizard dresses in an eccentric blend of reds, yellows, and oranges. His power is palpable, however: as one of Thentia's foremost archmages, he is largely responsible for keeping the Zhentarim and others at bay.
Orcs are aggressive humanoids that raid, pillage, and battle other creatures. They have a hatred of elves and dwarves that goes back many generations.
Orcus is a massive, bloated demon prince - bloated on bile and contempt. He is arguably the most vile being in the multiverse, and certainly one of the most powerful.
Orcus, Demon Prince of the Undead

The ogre-blooded Quah-Nomag is perhaps the most influential and powerful priest of Orcus alive today. Not only is Quah-Nomag despicable in every way, he was also instrumental in returning Orcus back to the living.

Wearers of Purple are members of the Cult of the Dragon who embrace the creation and veneration of the Sacred Ones, the great dracoliches of the Realms. Each Cult cell is led by one or more Wearers of Purple.

A tall, thin with a boisterous laugh, Cyril runs the Oxpit Tavern.
Ogres are ugly, greedy creatures who live by raiding and scavenging. They associate freely with Giants and Trolls, banding together to prey on the weak.

Tall, grim, with steely gray hair and blue eyes to match, Astar is every inch the formidable fighter. He's in perfect physical shape despite his forty-odd years. The warrior claims to be a wandering mercenary, but there is something in the way he carries himself, proud and commanding, that convinces you this wasn't always the case.
The typical Zhentarim fighter is a skilled warrior, cruel yet disciplined.

Deputy Chadee has a reputation for being one of the more fair-minded and even-handed of the Bron's deputies. She moves with deadly grace, wielding her katana - an unusual weapon in this part of the Realms.

A large, vicious-looking man, Dazel is the cruelest of the Bron's deputies, and as a result, a favorite of the Bron. Many of Voonlar's citizens have had the misfortune of being in the wrong place at the wrong time and subsequently ended up on the receiving end of Dazel's evil temper.
The deputy must have been incredibly drunk to have fallen asleep on the floor.
This huge man must be closer to seven feet tall than six, and he wields an axe that looks capable of cutting down a great oak in one or two swings.

This flame-haired deputy has a cruel sneer on her face. Deputy Jeyna holds a fearsome reputation in Voonlar for her skill with a crossbow, and has been said put a bolt through the head of an escaping prisoner from one hundred hundred yards.
Deputy Noric is the oldest of the Bron's deputies and is exceptionally quarrelsome as well as lazy. As such, he is well-suited to sentry duty.
This ranger appears unfriendly. She focuses on her comrade and all but ignores you.

Greater doppelgangers are the paranoid's ultimate nightmare: a monster who can eat your best friend's brain and then not only look like them, but talk like them, possess all of their memories, and wield all of their abilities.
Direguards are even more feared than Baneguards due to their ability to see invisible objects and creatures. Few rogues can evade detection by the Direguard.
Direguards are even more feared than Baneguards due to their ability to see invisible objects and creatures. Few rogues can evade detection by the Direguard.
This large, impressive man is the head priest of one of the most prominent temples of Tempus in the Realms. As such, he's a figure of no small power, both personal and political.
Dracoliches are undead dragons that have taken the path of immortality, gaining tremendous powers and abilities in the process.
This necromancer looks very old and very tired.

This bitter old drow is responsible for manufacturing the plentiful supply of potions the Innovator of Pain issues to the gladiators. His face is a ruined mess, a sight that would make even battle-hardened orcish barbarians grimace in disgust.
The drow are an evil subrace of elves, living deep underground in the dangerous Underdark.
The drow are an evil subrace of elves, living deep underground in the dangerous Underdark.

Druids of Mielikki dedicate their lives to the preservation and protection of the forests and woodlands. As a general rule, they are kindly and tolerant, but hate followers of the Beast Lord Malar with a passion.
This tired old noble reeks of drink.
Gargoyles are vicious predators that enjoy torturing weaker creatures. Their ability to perch indefinitely without moving causes adventurers to frequently mistake them for statues.
Whatever his true name once was, this orc's peculiar insistence on believing himself to be a child of Corellon Larethian has led to the other arena combatants referring to him mockingly as "Elf."
A typical citizen of Elventree. While many of the inhabitants of the small settlement are Harpers, rangers, or druids, a greater number are simple craftsmen, artists, or merchants.
A typical citizen of Elventree. While many of the inhabitants of the small settlement are Harpers, rangers, or druids, a greater number are simple craftsmen, artists, or merchants.
A sailor from one of the boats currently docked in Elmwood Harbor.

The typical ranger of Elventree is an excellent scout, superb tracker, and deadly archer. Although few in number, their skill is such that any would-be invaders think twice before attacking the small settlement.

Maganus dresses more like a disenfranchised noble than an archmage of prodigious power. Tall, grim, and seething with barely controlled fury, he is a man shaped by personal tragedy and driven by the single-minded pursuit of vengeance.
Crows are black birds known for their intelligence and adaptability.
This honest, plain-looking man runs the Still Waters Inn.
Sardonic, witty, and exceptionally handsome, Eremuth's elven blood is readily apparent in his bronzed skin and odd, gold-hued eyes.
Ezril the druid is in his late forties. He has a ragged cloth wrapped around his eyes, the result of some recent mishap.
Eremuth has taken the form of a mountain giant, the largest of giantkind. Unlike those dumb beasts, however, the eyes of this "giant" glimmer with a sinister intelligence.
The body of Ezril the druid has already begun collecting flies. His throat has been torn out - a ghastly sight.
Solars are the greatest of the celestials, usually close attendants to a deity, or champions of some cosmically beneficent task.
An icon of rugged individualism, yet renowned for its ability to hunt in packs, the noble Wolf is an animal of both mystique and power. This wolf, Fang, was a companion of the druid Ezril.

A devout priest of Ilmater, Father Garth has made it his calling to take on the burden of suffering from those in need. His kindly old face is crisscrossed by scars, and the way he limps speaks of broken bones that have never fully healed.
The Forsaken are sworn to guard the Ride with their lives.

Frost giants are justifiably feared as brutal and wantonly destructive raiders. They have the appearance of oversized, muscular humans with snow-white or ivory skin. These particular frost giants are more battle-hardened than their kin, and wear huge coats of chainmail armor over thick polar bear hide.

Fzoul is capable of anything. Quick-witted and a lover of power, he is dedicated to spreading tyranny across Faerûn. He rules Zhentil Keep and holds the titles of High Priest of the Temple of Bane and High Lord of the Zhentarim.
This young nobleman looks bewildered and angry.
A sad, broken prisoner, this gladiator isn't considered a threat and is therefore allowed to wander freely around the complex for the amusement of the Innovator of Pain.

This elf is battered and bruised, whip marks covering the exposed flesh on his back. If anything, he has been treated worse than the human prisoners. His face is set in a grim mask, but you see agony burning deep in his eyes.

Despite the toughness inherent in the dwarven race, this individual looks like he's born the weight of the world on his shoulders - and been crushed by it. He wanders around aimlessly, a glum expression on his face.

This frost giant female looks even more brutal than the males. The spear she was using as a makeshift ladle to stir the huge cook pot in the center of the room glows red hot.
This machination is clearly out of control.  Although quite powerful, its reasoning center is askew, and knows only combat and destruction.

Voonlar's high priest of Bane is a slender, cruel man of middling years. A good friend of the Bron, Gormstadd uses his position of influence within the Church of Bane to tyrannize the townsfolk and sow hatred wherever the opportunity arises.

This representative of the Shield is nearing his sixtieth year, and his wrinkled, weathered face seems fixed in a permanent frown.

A smooth, middle-aged man with a clarion voice, Hermuk is undeniably charismatic - a useful quality to have when one deals in wares that aren't always legal.

Hezrous are demonic sergeants, overseeing the formation of armies and commanding units in battle. They don't have the scheming instincts of the more powerful demons, but hezrous are cunning in battle.
The High Artificer is a quirky, eccentric man who, as well as leading the Purple Portals temple of Gond, is one of the foremost inventors in the Realms.
The crazed eyes of the High Priestess stare out hatefully above her veil. This is a woman with issues.
This stunning, red-haired woman is the high priestess of one of the Moonsea's wealthiest temples and hence a person of great influence in Thentia.
The High Priest of the Gate of Good Fortune is a short, wiry man with shoulder-length black hair.
High Whipmistress Suzildara Sharranen is a slender, stunning beauty with dark eyes and hair.

This elderly wizard's voluminous white robes are so large that they appear almost comical on his skinny frame. Only a fool would take him lightly however; Hilrad is widely considered one of the most intelligent and powerful wizards in Elventree. Fortunately, his power is matched by his kindness and good-natured eagerness to share his knowledge.
Despite his youth and small stature, this halfling looks as vicious as an angry tarrasque.
Huntmaster Baerdeth is a fit, intense man who paces back and forth like a predatory cat.
Ilandra Wavemistress is half sea elf, half human with deeply tanned skin and long, greenish-black hair.
The typical Zhentarim fighter is a skilled warrior, cruel yet disciplined.
This gnome looks preoccupied, as though constantly wrestling with problems only he can see.
This woman hides her face behind a hood, but her eyes are kind.
Like her sister, Jannatha is very short and slim. She is currently in a bad way, though not as bad as Baerimel.

The Red Plumes are the mercenary enforcers, soldiers and guards of Hillsfar, completely loyal to the city's evil wizard ruler Maalthiir -- as long as they are well paid.

Kalor Onehand is a tall, commanding figure wearing dark black plate mail and a permanent scowl. So named for his missing left hand, Kalor Onehand is nonetheless known to be one of the finest warriors in the Red Plume mercenary company.

Karandas stands seven feet tall, rippling muscles bulging beneath the thick red scales covering his body. Between his draconic heritage and the mighty greatsword he wields, the commander of the Order of the Crippled Fang looks every inch one of the most formidable warriors in the Realms.
This ranger is a huge bear of a man but seems friendly enough.
Kauvra is Orcus's vampiric enforcer. Her rages are infamous, as is the long list of creatures that she has slain single-handedly.

This tall, blonde, eyepatch-wearing woman seems half-crazed.
Kragdar is a monster of an ogre, taller than his fellows by a good head or more. He also appears to be decked out in powerful magical items most ogres could never dream of owning.
The admiral of Mulmaster's navy seems like a decent man, if a little uptight.

According to legend, countless lives have been lost attempting to breach the gates of Kur-Tharsu. Looking at the gates now, which stand as tall as a storm giant and appear sturdy enough to repel all but the most devastating attack, you know you will have your work cut out to break through.
This tall, pleasant woman is still attractive despite the passing years. Her raven black hair shows only a few hints of gray, and her dark brown eyes and easy smile make you feel immediately welcome.
Lana is still attractive despite the passing of the years, though her eyes hold a deep sadness.

A short-tempered, balding man of middling years, Laris isn't what one would expect of the owner of one of Faerun's largest magical shops. His aggressive temperament and incessant haggling ensure that he always gets the best side of any deal.
This young man looks terrified but determined. Whatever he's planning, he doesn't seem to have much confidence in his eventual success.
Lita is a delight to the eyes - a young elf woman in what seems to be her early twenties.

Lyressa's pallid skin is the only evidence of her condition. In fact, it would take an astute observer to recognize the absence of air being drawn into her lungs, or the slight odor of decay that her perfume cannot completely suppress.

Despite his deserved status as a ruthless tyrant, the merchant-wizard Maalthiir exhibits none of the casual cruelty or active malevolence his reputation might deem appropriate. Instead, he is a calm, even regal figure, with dark eyes that shine with wisdom and intelligence.
Madoc is bad-tempered, rude, and altogether poor company. In spite of that, he appears to be a very successful merchant.

The incredibly rare magic golem is a human-sized construct seemingly composed of iridescent yellow light. In fact, the being is formed from magic in its purest form. No spell, element, or enchanted weapon can wound the golem, for it will absorb any magic that comes into contact with it. For this reason, they are greatly feared by wizards and sorcerers.
The maid scurries back and forth like an ant, her face covered in a sheen of sweat.
This grimy fellow represents the worst of Voonlar's downtrodden citizenry.
The Red Plumes are the mercenary enforcers, soldiers and guards of Hillsfar, completely loyal to the city's evil wizard ruler Maalthiir - as long as they are well paid.
Melyrk Rubyripper is an energetic gnome with a wicked gleam in his eye and a love of haggling and bargains.
This fat, ruddy-faced merchant looks at his wit's end, both with his current predicament and his angry wife.
Priests of the Dark Lord Bane are feared throughout the Moonsea for their cruelty and love of strife.
This Zhentarim fighter is battered and covered in blood, his armor dented in innumerable places. Despite the obvious pain he is in, he somehow remains standing, swaying occasionally.

This shadowy figure is darkness incarnate, drinking the light of the nearby torches so that the entire area is plunged into blackness. Two glowing eyes are just about visible somewhere near the top of its wavering form.

An angry red glow surrounds this skeletal warrior. The ancient full plate shielding its yellowed bones is tarnished but uncracked, and the scimitars it clutches in both gauntleted fists look razor-sharp.

This foul creature strongly resembles a mummy, but without the stench of decay that normally accompanies the undead. Its right hand clutches a worn, blood-spattered whip, while its left hand is closed in to a fist.

The moon goddess Selûne typically manifests as trails of dancing motes of light, or 'moon motes'. Moondust blessed in a temple of Selûne creates motes of a similar appearance, which have the power to heal a variety of afflictions.
Exotically beautiful, yet as cold as a glacier, Nightshade carries herself with the confidence of one that can kill as effortlessly as she turns heads.
A nightwalker is a 20-foot-tall humanoid composed of pure darkness.
This blue-skinned djinni stands ten feet tall and boasts a muscular physique.

This merchant somehow manages to maintain a cheery demeanor despite being stuck in the middle of nowhere during the harshest winter the Moonsea has seen in years. Generous folk would call him a paragon of rugged stoicism. Others just point and shake their heads.
This old fellow looks as beaten-up as a three-legged dog. Nonetheless, his gap-toothed smile is genuine.
